e-7053.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of an Exponential Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
e-7053.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={t}^{2}+1\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=2t, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}={e}^{2t+1}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t=\int {e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t=\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =({t}^{2}+1)(\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2})(2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\int t\,{e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\displaystyle\int t\,e^{2t+1}\,\textrm{d}t.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=t\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}={e}^{2t+1}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t=\int {e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t=\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int t\,{e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =(t)(\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2})(1)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{t\,{e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{t\,{e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is a constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\int t\,{e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}}{2}-(\frac{t\,{e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}+D) \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\frac{t\,{e}^{2t+1}}{2}+\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}-D \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}(2{t}^{2}-2t+3)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C = -{D}.$ 

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t & ={[\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}(2{t}^{2}-2t+3)]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{{e}^{2(1)+1}}{4}(2(1)^{2}-2(1)+3))-(\frac{{e}^{2(0)+1}}{4}(2(0)^{2}-2(0)+3)) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3}}{4}(2-2+3)-\frac{e}{4}(0-0+3) \\  & =\frac{3{e}^{3}}{4}-\frac{3e}{4} \\  & =\frac{3{e}^{3}-3e}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

e-495.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of a Trigonometric Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
e-495.worked_solution:
In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={x}^{2} & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x) & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2})(\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))-\int (\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\frac{2}{3}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\displaystyle \int x\sin(3x) \textrm{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\text{d}x=-\,\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =x(-\,\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))-\int (-\,\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))\cdot 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\,\frac{1}{3}\,x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{3}\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x \\  & =-\,\frac{1}{3}\,x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{3}(\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))+{C}_{1} \\  & =-\,\frac{1}{3}\,x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{9}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+{C}_{1}\,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C_1$ is a constant of integration.
So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\frac{2}{3}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\frac{2}{3}(-\,\frac{1}{3}\,x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{9}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+{C}_{1}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\frac{2}{9}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-\frac{2}{27}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\frac{2{C}_{1}}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{27}((9{x}^{2}-2)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+6x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C = -\dfrac{2C_1}{3}.$

e-496.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of a Logarithmic Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
e-496.worked_solution:
We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2} & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=32{x}^{3} & \,⟹\,v=\int 32{x}^{3}\text{d}x=8{x}^{4}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 32{x}^{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & ={(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}(8{x}^{4})-\int (8{x}^{4})(\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x})\text{d}x \\  & =8{x}^{4}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-16\int {x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\displaystyle\int {x^3\ln(x)} \textrm{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x) & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={x}^{3} & \,⟹\,v=\int {x}^{3}\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)(\frac{{x}^{4}}{4})-\int (\frac{{x}^{4}}{4})(\frac{1}{x})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{4}-\frac{1}{4}\int {x}^{3}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{4}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{16}+{C}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

where $C_1$ is an integral constant. So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 32{x}^{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\text{d}x & =8{x}^{4}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-16\int {x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\text{d}x \\  & =8{x}^{4}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-16(\frac{{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{4}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{16}+{C}_{1}) \\  & =8{x}^{4}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-4{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+{x}^{4}-16{C}_{1} \\  & ={x}^{4}(8{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1)+C\,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C = -4C_1.$ Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}32{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\text{d}x & ={{x}^{4}(8{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1)|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =[(e)^{4}(8{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(e))}^{2}-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)+1)]-[(1)^{4}(8{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(1))}^{2}-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)+1)] \\  & =[{e}^{4}(8-4+1)]-1 \\  & =5{e}^{4}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 1
?

Calculate the integral ∫(1−2x2)e4xdx.

a
 e4x8(−4x2+2x+3)+C
b
 e4x4(4x2−2x+1)+C
c
e4x16(−8x2+4x+3)+C
d
 e4x16(−4x2+2x+1)+C
e
 e4x8(2x2+x+4)+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts twice gives (1-2x^2)e^{4x}/4 + xe^{4x}/4 - e^{4x}/16 + C = e^{4x}(-8x^2+4x+3)/16 + C. Differentiating this yields (1-2x^2)e^{4x}, confirming option c.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=1-2{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-4x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{4x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(1-2{x}^{2})(\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})-\int (\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})(-4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}}{4}+\int x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{4x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})-\int (\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{4x}}{4}-\frac{1}{4}\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{4x}}{4}-\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}+C \\  & =\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}(4x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{(1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}}{4}+(\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}(4x-1)+C) \\  & =\frac{(1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}}{4}+\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}(4x-1)+C \\  & =\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}(-8{x}^{2}+4x+3)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

Calculate the integral ∫(1−2x2)e4xdx.

a
 e4x8(−4x2+2x+3)+C
b
 e4x4(4x2−2x+1)+C
c
e4x16(−8x2+4x+3)+C
d
 e4x16(−4x2+2x+1)+C
e
 e4x8(2x2+x+4)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define u=1−2x2⟹dudx=−4xdvdx=e4x⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫e4xdx=e4x4.

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫(1−2x2)e4xdx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(1−2x2)(e4x4)−∫(e4x4)(−4x)dx=(1−2x2)e4x4+∫xe4xdx.

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate ∫xe4xdx. We take

u=x⟹dudx=1dvdx=e4x⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫e4xdx=e4x4.

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives ∫xe4xdx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=x(e4x4)−∫(e4x4)(1)dx=xe4x4−14∫e4xdx=xe4x4−e4x16+C=e4x16(4x−1)+C, where C is an integral constant.

content.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=1-2{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-4x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{4x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(1-2{x}^{2})(\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})-\int (\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})(-4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}}{4}+\int x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{4x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})-\int (\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{4x}}{4}-\frac{1}{4}\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{4x}}{4}-\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}+C \\  & =\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}(4x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{(1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}}{4}+(\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}(4x-1)+C) \\  & =\frac{(1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}}{4}+\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}(4x-1)+C \\  & =\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}(-8{x}^{2}+4x+3)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={x}^{2}+5\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{2x+2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{2x+2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{2x+2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({x}^{2}+5){e}^{2x+2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2}+5)(\frac{{e}^{2x+2}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2x+2}}{2})(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+5){e}^{2x+2}}{2}-\int x\,{e}^{2x+2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int x\,{e}^{2x+2}\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{2x+2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{2x+2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{2x+2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\,{e}^{2x+2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(x)(\frac{{e}^{2x+2}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2x+2}}{2})(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x\,{e}^{2x+2}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{2x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x\,{e}^{2x+2}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2x+2}}{4}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is a constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({x}^{2}+5){e}^{2x+2}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{({x}^{2}+5){e}^{2x+2}}{2}-\int x\,{e}^{2x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+5){e}^{2x+2}}{2}-(\frac{x\,{e}^{2x+2}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2x+2}}{4}+D) \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+5){e}^{2x+2}}{2}-\frac{x\,{e}^{2x+2}}{2}+\frac{{e}^{2x+2}}{4}-D \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x+2}}{4}(2{x}^{2}-2x+11)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-D.$ 

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}+5){e}^{2x+2}\,\text{d}x & ={[\frac{{e}^{2x+2}}{4}(2{x}^{2}-2x+11)]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{{e}^{2(1)+2}}{4}(2(1)^{2}-2(1)+11))-(\frac{{e}^{2(0)+2}}{4}(2(0)^{2}-2(0)+11)) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{4}}{4}(2-2+11)-\frac{{e}^{2}}{4}(0-0+11) \\  & =\frac{11{e}^{4}}{4}-\frac{11{e}^{2}}{4} \\  & =\frac{11{e}^{4}-11{e}^{2}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 3
?

Calculate ∫5x2e3xdx.

a
5e3x27(9x2−6x+2)+C
b
5e3x27(3x2−2x+1)+C
c
5e3x9(6x2−3x+1)+C
d
5e3x9(3x2+6x−2)+C
e
5e3x27(3x2+3x−2)+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts twice gives 5e^{3x}(x^2/3-2x/9+2/27)+C = 5e^{3x}(9x^2-6x+2)/27+C. Differentiating confirms the integrand 5x^2e^{3x}, so option a is correct.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=5{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=10x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{3x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 5{x}^{2}{e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(5{x}^{2})(\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3})-\int (\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3})(10x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5{x}^{2}{e}^{3x}}{3}-\frac{10}{3}\int x{e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int x{e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{3x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{3x}\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3})-\int (\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3})(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{3x}}{3}-\frac{1}{3}\int {e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{3x}}{3}-\frac{{e}^{3x}}{9}+D \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3x}}{9}(3x-1)+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 5{x}^{2}{e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{5{x}^{2}{e}^{3x}}{3}-\frac{10}{3}(\frac{{e}^{3x}}{9}(3x-1)+D) \\  & =\frac{5{x}^{2}{e}^{3x}}{3}-\frac{10{e}^{3x}}{27}(3x-1)-\frac{10D}{3} \\  & =\frac{5{e}^{3x}}{27}(9{x}^{2}-6x+2)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{10D}{3}.$

Question 3
?

Calculate ∫5x2e3xdx.

a
5e3x27(9x2−6x+2)+C
b
5e3x27(3x2−2x+1)+C
c
5e3x9(6x2−3x+1)+C
d
5e3x9(3x2+6x−2)+C
e
5e3x27(3x2+3x−2)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

u=5x2⟹dudx=10xdvdx=e3x⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫e3xdx=e3x3. Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫5x2e3xdx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(5x2)(e3x3)−∫(e3x3)(10x)dx=5x2e3x3−103∫xe3xdx.

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate ∫xe3xdx. We take

u=x⟹dudx=1dvdx=e3x⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫e3xdx=e3x3. In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives ∫xe3xdx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=x(e3x3)−∫(e3x3)(1)dx=xe3x3−13∫e3xdx=xe3x3−e3x9+D=e3x9(3x−1)+D, where D is an integral constant.

So we have

∫5x2e3xdx=5x2e3x3−103(e3x9(3x−1)+D)=5x2e3x3−10e3x27(3x−1)−10D3=5e3x27(9x2−6x+2)+C, where C=−10D3.

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of an Exponential Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
content.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=5{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=10x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{3x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 5{x}^{2}{e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(5{x}^{2})(\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3})-\int (\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3})(10x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5{x}^{2}{e}^{3x}}{3}-\frac{10}{3}\int x{e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int x{e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{3x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{3x}\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3})-\int (\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3})(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{3x}}{3}-\frac{1}{3}\int {e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{3x}}{3}-\frac{{e}^{3x}}{9}+D \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3x}}{9}(3x-1)+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 5{x}^{2}{e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{5{x}^{2}{e}^{3x}}{3}-\frac{10}{3}(\frac{{e}^{3x}}{9}(3x-1)+D) \\  & =\frac{5{x}^{2}{e}^{3x}}{3}-\frac{10{e}^{3x}}{27}(3x-1)-\frac{10D}{3} \\  & =\frac{5{e}^{3x}}{27}(9{x}^{2}-6x+2)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{10D}{3}.$

\begin{aligned}u={t}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=2t, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}={e}^{4t}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t=\int {e}^{4t}\,\text{d}t=\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4t}.\end{aligned}

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {t}^{2}{e}^{4t}\,\text{d}t & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =({t}^{2})(\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4t})-\int (\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4t})(2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{t}^{2}{e}^{4t}-\frac{1}{2}\int t{e}^{4t}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int t{e}^{4t}\,\text{d}t.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=t\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=1, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}={e}^{4t}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t=\int {e}^{4t}\,\text{d}t=\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4t}.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

Question 5
?

Calculate ∫(x2−4)exdx.

a
ex(x2−x+1)+C
b
ex(3x2−x−1)+C
c
ex(2x2−x+2)+C
d
ex(x2−2x−2)+C
e
ex(4x2−4x−1)+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts twice gives (x^2-4)e^x-2(xe^x-e^x)+C=e^x(x^2-2x-2)+C. Its derivative is e^x[(x^2-2x-2)+(2x-2)]=(x^2-4)e^x, confirming option d.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={x}^{2}-4\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x={e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({x}^{2}-4){e}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2}-4)({e}^{x})-\int ({e}^{x})(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2}-4){e}^{x}-2\int x{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int x{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x={e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x({e}^{x})-\int ({e}^{x})(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{e}^{x}-\int {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{e}^{x}-{e}^{x}+D \\  & ={e}^{x}(x-1)+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({x}^{2}-4){e}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =({x}^{2}-4){e}^{x}-2({e}^{x}(x-1)+D) \\  & =({x}^{2}-4){e}^{x}-2(x-1){e}^{x}-2D \\  & ={e}^{x}({x}^{2}-2x-2)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-2D.$

Question 5
?

Calculate ∫(x2−4)exdx.

a
ex(x2−x+1)+C
b
ex(3x2−x−1)+C
c
ex(2x2−x+2)+C
d
ex(x2−2x−2)+C
e
ex(4x2−4x−1)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define u=x2−4⟹dudx=2xdvdx=ex⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫exdx=ex.

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫(x2−4)exdx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(x2−4)(ex)−∫(ex)(2x)dx=(x2−4)ex−2∫xexdx.

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate ∫xexdx. We take

u=x⟹dudx=1dvdx=ex⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫exdx=ex.

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives ∫xexdx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=x(ex)−∫(ex)(1)dx=xex−∫exdx=xex−ex+D=ex(x−1)+D, where D is an integral constant.

So we have ∫(x2−4)exdx=(x2−4)ex−2(ex(x−1)+D)=(x2−4)ex−2(x−1)ex−2D=ex(x2−2x−2)+C, where C=−2D.

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of an Exponential Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
content.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={x}^{2}-4\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x={e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$

$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 1\,dx \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,dx \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-6\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-6(-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+D) \\  & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+6x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C,\end{aligned}

content.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(3{x}^{2})(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))(6x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-6\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 1\,dx \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,dx \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-6\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-6(-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+D) \\  & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+6x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-6D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & ={[3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+6x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(3(\pi )^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )+6(\pi )\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ))-(3(0)^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+6(0)\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)) \\  & =0+6\pi (-1)-0-0 \\  & =-6\pi \end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts twice gives x^2 sin(x-1)+2x cos(x-1)-2 sin(x-1)+C. Combining the sine terms yields option c. Differentiation cancels the extra terms and leaves x^2 cos(x-1).

after.name: Question 8
after.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. 

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2})(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1))-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)-2\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(x)(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1))(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)+\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)\,\text{d}x & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)-2(-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)+D) \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)-2D \\  & =({x}^{2}-2)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-2D.$

EXPLANATION

We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define u=x2⟹dudx=2xdvdx=cos⁡(x−1)⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫cos⁡(x−1)dx=sin⁡(x−1).

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫x2cos⁡(x−1)dx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(x2)(sin⁡(x−1))−∫(sin⁡(x−1)(2x)dx=x2sin⁡(x−1)−2∫xsin⁡(x−1)dx.

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate ∫xsin⁡(x−1)dx. We take u=x⟹dudx=1dvdx=sin⁡(x−1)⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫sin⁡(x−1)dx=−cos⁡(x−1).

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives ∫xsin⁡(x−1)dx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(x)(−cos⁡(x−1))−∫(−cos⁡(x−1))(1)dx=−xcos⁡(x−1)+∫cos⁡(x−1)dx=−xcos⁡(x−1)+sin⁡(x−1)+D, where D is an integral constant.

So we have ∫x2cos⁡(x−1)dx=x2sin⁡(x−1)−2(−xcos⁡(x−1)+sin⁡(x−1)+D)=x2sin⁡(x−1)+2xcos⁡(x−1)−2sin⁡(x−1)−2D=(x2−2)sin⁡(x−1)+2xcos⁡(x−1)+C, where C=−2D.

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of a Trigonometric Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
content.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. 

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2})(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1))-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)-2\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(x)(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1))(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)+\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)\,\text{d}x & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)-2(-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)+D) \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)-2D \\  & =({x}^{2}-2)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-1)+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-2D.$

decision.explanation: Take u=x^2 and dv=sin(3x) dx, so du=2x dx and v=-cos(3x)/3. Integration by parts gives -x^2 cos(3x)/3+(2/3)∫x cos(3x) dx, matching option e.

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. 

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2})(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{2}{3}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define u=x2⟹dudx=2xdvdx=sin⁡(3x)⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫sin⁡(3x)dx=−cos⁡(3x)3.

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫x2sin⁡(3x)dx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(x2)(−cos⁡(3x)3)−∫(−cos⁡(3x)3)(2x)dx=−x2cos⁡(3x)3+23∫xcos⁡(3x)dx.

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of a Trigonometric Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
content.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. 

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2})(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{2}{3}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=({log}_{2}⁡x)^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2{log}_{2}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=9{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int 9{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=3{x}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 9{x}^{2}({log}_{2}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={({log}_{2}⁡x)}^{2}(3{x}^{3})-\int (3{x}^{3})(\frac{2{log}_{2}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{3}{({log}_{2}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{6}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int {x}^{2}{log}_{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate  $\int {x}^{2}{log}_{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{2}⁡x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}{log}_{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{2}⁡x)(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})-\int (\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}{log}_{2}⁡x}{3}-\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}{log}_{2}⁡x}{3}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{9\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 9{x}^{2}({log}_{2}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =3{x}^{3}{({log}_{2}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{6}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(\frac{{x}^{3}{log}_{2}⁡x}{3}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{9\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+D) \\  & =3{x}^{3}{({log}_{2}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2{x}^{3}{log}_{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3{ln}^{2}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{3}{ln}^{2}⁡x}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}-\frac{2{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}+\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3{ln}^{2}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}(3{ln}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\frac{2}{3})+C.\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{6D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{2}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}9{x}^{2}({log}_{2}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & ={[\frac{{x}^{3}}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}(3{ln}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\frac{2}{3})]}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3}}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}(3{ln}^{2}⁡e-2\operatorname{ln}⁡e+\frac{2}{3})-\frac{{1}^{3}}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}(3{ln}^{2}⁡1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡1+\frac{2}{3}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3}}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}(3-2+\frac{2}{3})-\frac{1}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}(0-0+\frac{2}{3}) \\  & =\frac{5{e}^{3}}{3{ln}^{2}⁡2}-\frac{2}{3{ln}^{2}⁡2} \\  & =\frac{5{e}^{3}-2}{3{ln}^{2}⁡2}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 9{x}^{2}({log}_{2}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={({log}_{2}⁡x)}^{2}(3{x}^{3})-\int (3{x}^{3})(\frac{2{log}_{2}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{3}{({log}_{2}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{6}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int {x}^{2}{log}_{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}

$$

So we have

$$

$$

where $C=-\frac{6D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{2}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}9{x}^{2}({log}_{2}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & ={[\frac{{x}^{3}}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}(3{ln}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\frac{2}{3})]}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3}}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}(3{ln}^{2}⁡e-2\operatorname{ln}⁡e+\frac{2}{3})-\frac{{1}^{3}}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}(3{ln}^{2}⁡1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡1+\frac{2}{3}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3}}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}(3-2+\frac{2}{3})-\frac{1}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}(0-0+\frac{2}{3}) \\  & =\frac{5{e}^{3}}{3{ln}^{2}⁡2}-\frac{2}{3{ln}^{2}⁡2} \\  & =\frac{5{e}^{3}-2}{3{ln}^{2}⁡2}.\end{aligned}

We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3})\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{6\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3}))(x)-\int (x)(\frac{6\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3})-6\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3}))(x)-\int (x)(\frac{3}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})-3\int \text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})-3x+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is a constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & =x{ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3})-6(x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})-3x+D) \\  & =x{ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3})-6x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})+18x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-6D.$ 

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}{ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & ={[x{ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3})-6x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})+18x]}_{1}^{e} \\  & =[e{ln}^{2}⁡({e}^{3})-6e\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{3})+18e]-[(1){ln}^{2}⁡({1}^{3})-6(1)\operatorname{ln}⁡({1}^{3})+18(1)] \\  & =9e-18e+18e-18 \\  & =9e-18.\end{aligned}

Evaluate ∫1e(log3⁡(x2))2dx.

b

c

d

e

decision.explanation: Since log₃(x²)=2ln(x)/ln(3), the integral is 4/(ln(3))² times ∫₁ᵉ(ln(x))² dx. Integration by parts twice gives x[(ln(x))²-2ln(x)+2], whose endpoint difference is e-2. Thus the answer is (4e-8)/(ln(3))², option c.

after.name: Question 13
after.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{4{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}-\int (x)(\frac{4{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}-\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int {log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate  $\int {log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))(x)-\int (x)(\frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})-\frac{2x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}\,\text{d}x & =x{({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}-\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(x{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})-\frac{2x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D) \\  & =x{({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}-\frac{4x{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+\frac{8x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{x{ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{2})}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}-\frac{4x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+\frac{8x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}({ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{2})-4\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})+8)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{4D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}{({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}\,\text{d}x & ={[\frac{x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}({ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{2})-4\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})+8)]}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{e}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}({ln}^{2}⁡({e}^{2})-4\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})+8)-\frac{1}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}({ln}^{2}⁡({1}^{2})-4\operatorname{ln}⁡({1}^{2})+8) \\  & =\frac{e}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(4-8+8)-\frac{1}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(0-0+8) \\  & =\frac{4e-8}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{4{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}-\int (x)(\frac{4{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}-\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int {log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate  $\int {log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))(x)-\int (x)(\frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})-\frac{2x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}\,\text{d}x & =x{({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}-\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(x{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})-\frac{2x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D) \\  & =x{({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}-\frac{4x{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+\frac{8x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{x{ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{2})}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}-\frac{4x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+\frac{8x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}({ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{2})-4\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})+8)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{4D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}{({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}\,\text{d}x & ={[\frac{x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}({ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{2})-4\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})+8)]}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{e}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}({ln}^{2}⁡({e}^{2})-4\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})+8)-\frac{1}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}({ln}^{2}⁡({1}^{2})-4\operatorname{ln}⁡({1}^{2})+8) \\  & =\frac{e}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(4-8+8)-\frac{1}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(0-0+8) \\  & =\frac{4e-8}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

Calculate the integral ∫(log3⁡x)2dx.

a
x((log3⁡x)2−3log3⁡(x)ln⁡3+3ln2⁡3)+C
b
x((log3⁡x)2−2log3⁡(x)ln⁡3+2ln2⁡3)+C
c
2x((log3⁡x)2−log3⁡(x)ln⁡3−1ln2⁡3)+C
d
x((log3⁡x)2+2log3⁡(x)ln⁡3−2ln2⁡3)+C
e
2x(3(log3⁡x)2+log3⁡(x)ln⁡3+2ln2⁡3)+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Using log₃(x)=ln(x)/ln(3), integration by parts twice gives x[(ln(x))²-2ln(x)+2]/(ln(3))²+C. Rewriting in base 3 matches option b.

after.name: Question 15
after.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}(x)-\int (x)(\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int {log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate  $\int {log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{3}⁡(x))(x)-\int (x)(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{3}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{3}⁡(x)-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =x{({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(x{log}_{3}⁡(x)-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D) \\  & =x{({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2x{log}_{3}⁡(x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+\frac{2x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}-\frac{2D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =x({({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡(x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+\frac{2}{{ln}^{2}⁡3})+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{2D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

after.html:
Question 15
?

Calculate the integral ∫(log3⁡x)2dx.

a
x((log3⁡x)2−3log3⁡(x)ln⁡3+3ln2⁡3)+C
b
x((log3⁡x)2−2log3⁡(x)ln⁡3+2ln2⁡3)+C
c
2x((log3⁡x)2−log3⁡(x)ln⁡3−1ln2⁡3)+C
d
x((log3⁡x)2+2log3⁡(x)ln⁡3−2ln2⁡3)+C
e
2x(3(log3⁡x)2+log3⁡(x)ln⁡3+2ln2⁡3)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define u=(log3⁡x)2⟹dudx=2log3⁡xxln⁡3dvdx=1⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫dx=x.

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫(log3⁡x)2dx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(log3⁡x)2(x)−∫(x)(2log3⁡xxln⁡3)dx=x(log3⁡x)2−2ln⁡3∫log3⁡(x)dx.

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate ∫log3⁡(x)dx. We take u=log3⁡(x)⟹dudx=1xln⁡3dvdx=1⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫dx=x.

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives ∫log3⁡(x)dx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(log3⁡(x))(x)−∫(x)(1xln⁡3)dx=xlog3⁡(x)−1ln⁡3∫dx=xlog3⁡(x)−xln⁡3+D, where D is an integral constant.

So we have ∫(log3⁡x)2dx=x(log3⁡x)2−2ln⁡3(xlog3⁡(x)−xln⁡3+D)=x(log3⁡x)2−2xlog3⁡(x)ln⁡3+2xln2⁡3−2Dln⁡3=x((log3⁡x)2−2log3⁡(x)ln⁡3+2ln2⁡3)+C, where C=−2Dln⁡3.

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of a Logarithmic Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
content.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}(x)-\int (x)(\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int {log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate  $\int {log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{3}⁡(x))(x)-\int (x)(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{3}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{3}⁡(x)-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =x{({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(x{log}_{3}⁡(x)-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D) \\  & =x{({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2x{log}_{3}⁡(x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+\frac{2x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}-\frac{2D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =x({({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡(x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+\frac{2}{{ln}^{2}⁡3})+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{2D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$
